note: Appendix B row 10's runs (card#7342 step 10): the drill-down opened from the floor — AT-D3-4, AT-D3-16, and the panel halves of AT-D3-6, AT-D3-10 and AT-D3-14. Every seat object is lifted from the fixture its run names (`fx-snapshot-4`, `fx-nulls`, `fx-interns`, `fx-collision`); the detail and timeline bodies carry the columns `FleetController` serves, in its envelope order.

panel_feed_dies.note: AT-D3-6's PANEL half: `feed_dies` (fx-snapshot-4's floor-half run, unchanged) with the drill-down opened on `aimla-pm` at 1 s. The detail and timeline responses are `clocked`, like every poll of the silence, so each carries the server's own instant. Every poll answers `aimla-pm` at the SAME `state_version` the client holds, which the protocol drops under § 2.2's version rule — and whose `fetch-fresh` blocks are fresher readings of that one state, which is what re-stamps the panel's blocks (§ 2.4's stamp rule).

panel_feed_lives.note: AT-D3-6's panel-half CONTROL: `feed_lives` with the drill-down opened on `aimla-pm` at 1 s. No poll is ever issued, so nothing re-delivers the `fetch-fresh` blocks and their stamp is the detail response's for the whole run.

panel_ages.note: AT-D3-10's PANEL half: fx-snapshot-4 on the floor, the drill-down opened on `aimla-pm` at 1 s. The detail response is read 900 ms after the snapshot on the server's clock. The test sets the browser clock (`browser_clock_ms`) — correct for the control, +3 h for the GREEN and the RED.

panel_nulls.note: AT-D3-14's PANEL half: `fx-nulls` on the floor, the drill-down opened on `nulls-a` at 0.5 s, closed at 1.5 s, and opened on `nulls-b` at 2 s. `nulls-a`'s detail carries no open call at all and NULL counter snapshots (the reporter has never heartbeat), so its intern list has nothing to list; `nulls-b`'s carries its one untitled, untyped dispatch and its own call.

panel_real_zero.note: AT-D3-14's discriminating control, on the panel: `fx-nulls`' `real_zero` seat — a context sample that MEASURED 0.0 % — opened in the drill-down. A real zero draws a bar at 0 %, where a null draws none.

panel_interns.note: AT-D3-4: `fx-interns` (0 → 8 → 8-with-`subagents_open`-9) on the floor, then the drill-down opened on `aimla-interns` at 2.5 s against a detail response carrying NINE open dispatch calls — the ninth titled null — beside the seat's own `Bash` call.

retire_message_first.note: AT-D3-16, the announcement in the MESSAGE-first order § 2.5 says either arrives in: fx-snapshot-4 on the floor with the drill-down open on `aimla-review`, the two announcements of its retirement 0.5 s apart, then the stream ends and the recovery's poll answers a later snapshot that no longer lists the seat. The delta's `retired` member names an operator (`by`); the message carries none, as D2 § 8.3 declares.

retire_delta_first.note: AT-D3-16, the announcement in the DELTA-first order § 2.5 says either arrives in: fx-snapshot-4 on the floor with the drill-down open on `aimla-review`, the two announcements of its retirement 0.5 s apart, then the stream ends and the recovery's poll answers a later snapshot that no longer lists the seat. The delta's `retired` member names an operator (`by`); the message carries none, as D2 § 8.3 declares.

retire_collision.note: AT-D3-16's collision chain: § 3.3's worked collision (`fx-collision`'s `collision` run — `aimla-impl-4` arrives, takes slot 0, and `aimla-pm` probes to slot 1), then `aimla-impl-4` is retired by the message alone. `aimla-pm` moves back into the freed slot and no other desk moves.

retire_backstop.note: AT-D3-16's BACKSTOP (§ 2.3 row 4), and its control. fx-snapshot-4 on the floor; a heartbeat at 1 s counts 3 seats while the client holds 4, so the one discovery fetch it triggers reads a snapshot that omits `aimla-review` — a seat NO announcement was ever made about. Then the absences that must remove nothing: `aimla-impl-2` goes `stale` then `offline`, and `aimla-pm` takes a delta gap whose resync answers ONE seat object.
